A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same two-stage face-decomposition work. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement, although both refer to supplementary implementation details and v2 places its H3DS evaluation there. The included material supports comparison, but those supplementary components cannot be checked.

before.justification: v1 reports original FaceScape reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and rendering and relighting results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reconstruction experiments and reports additional ablations and diffuse/specular evaluation results in Tables 2 and 3.

M1.justification: v2 adds an albedo-gradient predictor trained during Stage 1 with a new supervised loss, Lg. Its output becomes an additional input to both the geometry-displacement and BRDF-offset networks in Stage 2 (Sections 4.1–4.3). This changes the learned facial prior, training objective, and refinement procedure.

E1.justification: FaceScape reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, editing, and relighting coverage remains. v2 Section 5.1 additionally reports using H3DS to assess generalization. Its supplementary evaluation is absent from the supplied PDFs, so the specific population, conditions, and outcomes cannot be verified.

E2.justification: The five Table 1 baselines remain unchanged. RefMM, previously only cited, is now run on test images and discussed as a qualitative comparison in Section 5.4 and Figure 6. It also supplies pseudo ground truth; the new quantitative Table 3 compares the proposed method with NeuFace.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation of diffuse and specular SSIM against RefMM-generated pseudo ground truth, while removing v1's empty-specular-output failure metric. The reported FaceScape subject counts, 3/5/10-view settings, optimizer, and training budget remain unchanged. Newly specified held-out views and preprocessing are additional disclosures.

E4.justification: Table 2 expands beyond the original synergy and scattering ablations to test removing the entire facial template and the albedo-gradient predictor. This directly tests previously unablated Stage 1 contributions. Section 5.4 adds reflectance-quality analysis against pseudo references, while v1's view-dependent specular-failure analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The changed failure-rate and SSIM reporting concerns experimental outcomes rather than uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: All 72 Table 1 values and the original Table 2 rows are unchanged. v2 adds two ablation rows and Table 3: diffuse/specular SSIM is 0.761/0.692 for the proposed method versus 0.726/0.552 for NeuFace. It removes v1's specular-failure results: 0% for the proposed method and 30%/25%/20% for NeuFace at 3/5/10 views.

T1.justification: v2 introduces the albedo-gradient target and its supervised loss, incorporating the predictor into the mathematical model in Equations 7, 8, and 10. The existing BRDF, SDF, and scattering formulations largely remain. v1's explicit volume-rendering Equation 4 is omitted; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about two-stage decomposition, reconstruction from three views, and relighting/editing remain. v2's introduction adds a contribution claim for an albedo-gradient predictor that captures more general facial reflectance priors.

C2.justification: v2 explains how albedo gradients address skin-color variation and deviations from the facial template. It explicitly disclaims physically accurate reflectance decomposition and attributes low SSIM to coarse pseudo ground truth. The conclusion removes v1's specific limitation concerning intricate geometry such as teeth.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents ImFace-based face-mask preprocessing, ten held-out test views, and consistent independent test data across methods. The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a project-page address. The PDFs do not establish whether code is available at that address.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the separate geometry-from-neural-fields survey and substantially expands positioning against monocular morphable-face methods and video or polarized-image capture. Added references include MoSAR, FitMe, Relightify, and SunStage. The discussion now explicitly distinguishes input and reflectance-supervision requirements from the proposed sparse-view approach.

P1.justification: The paper receives the SFDM name and a revised title, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, and explanatory method prose. Related work is reorganized, geometry-displacement and BRDF-offset descriptions are combined, and a separate reflectance-analysis section precedes the renumbered applications section.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the opening illustration and revises the pipeline, removes v1's framework overview and standalone NeuFace diagnostic, and combines the BRDF and scattering diagrams. It expands the ablation display, adds a RefMM figure and Table 3, adds Table 1's Relight column, and reorganizes the application illustrations.

improvement.justification: The existing facial-template contribution now receives direct ablation evidence, and the new gradient predictor has its own control. Added preprocessing and test-split details improve reproducibility, while the qualified reflectance analysis broadens validation. Removing the specular-failure diagnostic and teeth limitation loses useful transparency, and the pseudo references cannot establish physical accuracy. Overall, the supported gains are limited but positive.
